# modgrad-obs

> Training observability for LLM pre-, mid- and post-training runs: metrics,
> events and summaries stored as append-only JSONL, a live dashboard, and
> analysis (trends, honest forecasts, spikes, divergence, seed noise) that
> runs in the client, never on the server. This file is the quickstart for
> coding agents. It is complete: you should not need anything else.

## Setting up a repo: done means a run the user can open

When a user asks you to add modgrad to a repo (set it up, track or log
their training, show them a dashboard), the job is finished only when their
training has run once through modgrad and you have told them how to open
it:

1. `modgrad init` in the repo (`modgrad init --server <url>` if they named a
   server). It lists the training scripts it found and the exact command
   for each.
2. Run the training once, unchanged except as below:
   - the script prints metrics (`step 10 loss 0.52`, Trainer dicts, ...):
     `modgrad run --name <name> -- python <script>`. No code change.
   - the script uses wandb: change only the line `import wandb` to
     `import modgrad as wandb`, in place, without retyping the file:
     `perl -pi -e 's/^import wandb$/import modgrad as wandb/' <script>`.
     Then run it as usual (`python <script>`); the `wandb.init/log/finish`
     calls stay as they are.
   - the script prints nothing: add one print per logging step (see
     "2. modgrad run"). Read the file first; never rewrite or replace the
     user's training code.
3. Check that the run has rows: `modgrad tail <name>`. It exits non-zero
   with "no rows yet" when nothing was logged: then the training did not
   run under modgrad, and you are not done.
4. Answer with the way to open it. Local mode: the command
   `modgrad-server --root obs` and the URL to open once it is up,
   `http://127.0.0.1:8790/`. Do not start `modgrad-server` yourself: it
   serves until stopped, so your command never returns. Server mode: the
   run's link that `modgrad run` printed when it ended
   (`<server>/#run=...`). The project page `modgrad init` prints is empty
   until a run logs, so it is not an answer on its own.

Never commit `.modgrad.json` (it can hold a token; `init` gitignores it)
and never paste a token into a tracked file.

Binaries: `modgrad` (CLI and MCP server) and `modgrad-server` (HTTP API, dashboard).
If `modgrad --version` works, they are installed; skip this step.
Install from a checkout of https://github.com/rotkonetworks/modgrad:

    cargo install --path crates/modgrad-obs          # -> modgrad
    cargo install --path crates/modgrad-obs-server   # -> modgrad-server
    pip install ./clients/python                     # optional: import modgrad as wandb

## Start here: modgrad init

Run this once in the user's project directory. It never prompts and is safe
to re-run.

    modgrad init                                     # local: runs go to ./obs, no server, no account
    modgrad init --server https://obs.example.org    # a modgrad-server: gets an anonymous project token
    modgrad init --mcp claude                        # also register the MCP server in .mcp.json (Claude Code)
    modgrad init --json                              # the result as one JSON object on stdout

It writes `.modgrad.json` (server, project and token, or the local data
dir) and adds it to `.gitignore` (local mode also ignores `obs/`); the output
says when `.gitignore` changed. `--mcp cursor` writes `.cursor/mcp.json`.
It ends by printing the next steps:

    modgrad run --name exp1 -- python train.py       # wrap a script that prints metrics
    modgrad tail exp1                                # latest values and sparklines
    modgrad-server --root obs                        # local mode: then open http://127.0.0.1:8790/

Python logs with no further setup (`pip install ./clients/python`):

    import modgrad as wandb
    wandb.init(name="exp1", config={"lr": 3e-4})
    wandb.log({"loss": 0.52})

In local mode this writes `obs/runs/exp1/` directly, in the same format as
`modgrad run --offline`, and prints
`modgrad: run exp1 -> obs/runs/exp1 (view: modgrad-server --root obs)`.
With a server it logs to the file's project. `init(project="sweep")` puts the
run in `obs/runs/sweep/exp1`; a name that is already taken gets a `-<4 hex>`
suffix, and `init(id="exp1", resume=True)` continues a run after its last
step. Each `log` call is appended to disk at once, so a killed script still
leaves a readable run. `mode="offline"` (or `WANDB_MODE=offline`) writes
locally whatever the project file says. A script that uses the client and
is started by `modgrad run --name X` logs into run X (one run, not two).

`modgrad run`, `tail`, `mcp` and the Python client find `.modgrad.json` in
the current directory or a parent. Precedence: flag > environment variable >
`.modgrad.json` > default. The token in it is only sent to the server it
names. `MODGRAD_URL` picks a server and `MODGRAD_DATA` a local obs
directory, whatever the file says.

Data lives in an obs directory (default `./obs`): `obs/runs/<run>/` holds
`config.json`, `metrics.jsonl`, `arrays.jsonl` (histograms, tensors),
`events.jsonl`, `summary.json`. Run names are
1 to 3 `/`-separated parts of `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`, e.g. `sweep/lr3e-4_s1`.
Name seeds `<config>_s1`, `<config>_s2`, ...: the tools group them and test
differences against seed noise.

## The doors

Every door ends in the same place: a run with metrics you can query and chart.

1. MCP: `modgrad mcp`. An agent reads and writes runs through 7 tools. Use this
   to answer questions about runs ("did it diverge?", "worth continuing?").
2. `modgrad run -- <command>`: wraps a training command, passes its output through
   unchanged, parses metric lines from stdout/stderr, and samples CPU/RSS/GPU.
   No code change. Use this to instrument a script that already prints metrics.
3. HTTP API: `POST $OBS/api/v1/runs/<run>/log` with JSON. Any language, no
   client library. Use this inside a training loop or framework callback.
4. The dashboard: `modgrad-server` serves it at `/`. `$OBS/#new` creates an
   anonymous project and shows ready-to-paste commands; `#run=<id>`,
   `#project=<p>` and `#board=<id>` open a run, a project or a saved board.
   Log files (CSV, JSONL, text logs, TensorBoard, W&B offline) can also be
   dropped onto the page.
5. SSH, the zero-install alternative (servers started with `--ssh`):
   `python train.py 2>&1 | ssh <host>`. See "SSH" below.

## 1. MCP

After `modgrad init`, plain `modgrad mcp` uses the project file: its server
(with its token) or its local data dir. `modgrad init --mcp claude` registers
exactly that. Explicitly:

Local data (recommended; nothing else to run):

    modgrad mcp --dir ./obs                                        # or MODGRAD_DATA=./obs

Against a modgrad-server (the tools fetch rows and analyse locally; the server
only stores and selects):

    modgrad mcp --url https://obs.example.org --token obsp_...    # or MODGRAD_MCP_URL=... MODGRAD_TOKEN=...

A server started with `modgrad-server --mcp` also serves MCP over streamable HTTP
at `$OBS/mcp`. That is for agents that cannot run a local binary: the
analysis then runs on the server. Prefer `modgrad mcp --url` when you can.

Claude Code:

    claude mcp add modgrad -- modgrad mcp --dir ./obs
    claude mcp add --scope project modgrad -- modgrad mcp --dir obs          # writes .mcp.json
    claude mcp add modgrad --env MODGRAD_TOKEN=obsp_... -- modgrad mcp --url https://obs.example.org
    claude mcp add --transport http modgrad https://obs.example.org/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer obsp_..."

Cursor (`.cursor/mcp.json`) and any client that takes the common JSON shape
(`.mcp.json`, Claude Desktop, Windsurf, Cline, ...):

    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "modgrad": { "command": "modgrad", "args": ["mcp", "--dir", "obs"] }
      }
    }

Remote store, local analysis:

    { "mcpServers": { "modgrad": { "command": "modgrad", "args": ["mcp", "--url", "https://obs.example.org"],
                               "env": { "MODGRAD_TOKEN": "obsp_..." } } } }

Hosted endpoint (only if the agent cannot run `modgrad`):

    { "mcpServers": { "modgrad": { "url": "https://obs.example.org/mcp",
                               "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer obsp_..." } } } }

Tools (arguments are flat and forgiving; run and metric names are fuzzy):

    list_runs(filter?)                    runs with last step, metric count, status
    read_metric(run, metric, last?)       recent values, min/max/last, NaN/inf warning
    summarize(run, metric?, target?)      Verdict line (DIVERGED / OVERFITTING / improving /
                                          no clear progress), trend, spikes and what changed
                                          before them, honest forecast ("no skill" when it
                                          cannot beat the last value), ETA to target, seeds
    compare(runs, metric)                 aligned table, best run, diverged runs; seed groups
                                          (x_s1, x_s2, ...) get mean ± sd and WITHIN/BEYOND noise
    log(run, metrics, step?)              record values; creates the run
    ingest_log(run, text)                 parse pasted stdout into a run
    make_board(query)                     save a dashboard board, return its URL;
                                          query = metric{run=~"a|b"}; several panels with ';'.
                                          Local data: the URL is for `modgrad-server --root <dir>`
                                          (it says so); --base-url or the project file's server
                                          changes it

Typical calls:

    summarize(run="sweep/lr3e-4")                         "is it worth continuing?"
    compare(runs="sweep/*", metric="val_loss")            "which run diverged?"
    compare(runs="abl/base_s*,abl/wd_s*", metric="val_loss")   "is the difference real?"
    summarize(run="long/a", metric="val_loss", target=2.0)     "when will it reach 2.0?"
    make_board(query='reward{run=~"rl/ppo_a|rl/ppo_b"}; kl{run=~"rl/ppo_a|rl/ppo_b"}')

Report what the tools say. If summarize says the forecast has "no skill",
do not give a confident number.

## 2. modgrad run

    modgrad run --offline --name exp1 -- python train.py      # writes ./obs/runs/exp1
    modgrad run --name exp1 -- python train.py                # streams to $MODGRAD_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:8790)
    modgrad run --server https://obs.example.org --token obsp_... --project team --name exp1 -- torchrun ...

Lines it understands (one metric line per print is enough):

    step 1250: loss 3.48 acc 7.5%
    iter 100 | loss=2.31 | lr 3e-4
    [epoch 2/10] train_loss: 0.45
    {'loss': 0.41, 'learning_rate': 5e-05, 'epoch': 0.3}     (HF Trainer's default output)
    tqdm postfixes: 100%|####| 500/500 [00:12<00:00, loss=0.31]

A line without a step uses the last step seen. The child's exit code is
returned. If the server is unreachable, rows are spooled to disk and
`modgrad push <spool dir>` resends them. `modgrad tail <run>` prints the latest
values with sparklines.

Transport: with an https server that advertises HTTP/3 (`Alt-Svc: h3`),
`modgrad run` and `push` send rows over QUIC (UDP), else over TCP. If UDP is
blocked (common on HPC clusters and corporate networks), the handshake gives
up after 1.5 s and the run continues over TCP for the rest of the process.
One line says which: `modgrad: pushing over HTTP/3 (udp ...)` or
`modgrad: pushing over HTTPS (UDP blocked, fell back: ...)`. `--h3` tries
HTTP/3 even for an http:// URL, `--no-h3` (or `MODGRAD_H3=0`) never tries it,
and `--tls-ca <pem>` trusts a dev server's self-signed certificate. The spool
works the same over either. curl, browsers and the Python client use TCP.

To instrument a silent script: add one print per logging step, e.g.
`print(f"step {step} loss={loss:.6f} lr={lr:.3e}", flush=True)`, then wrap it
with `modgrad run`.

## 3. HTTP API

Full reference, plain text: `curl $OBS/api/v1`. Bodies are JSON whatever the
Content-Type; errors are JSON with a corrected example. A server started with
`--h3 <udp addr>` also serves the same API over HTTP/3; TCP always works.

    modgrad-server --root obs --dev                     # local server; --dev = writes need no token
    curl -X POST $OBS/api/v1/projects               # -> {"project", "token": "obsp_...", "board"}
    curl -X POST $OBS/api/v1/runs/exp1/log -H "Authorization: Bearer $MODGRAD_TOKEN" \
         -d '{"step": 10, "loss": 0.52, "acc": "71.5%"}'
    curl -X POST $OBS/api/v1/runs/exp1/log -H "Authorization: Bearer $MODGRAD_TOKEN" \
         -d '{"rows": [{"step": 11, "loss": 0.5}], "events": ["lr drop"], "config": {"lr": 3e-4}}'
    python train.py 2>&1 | curl -X POST $OBS/api/v1/runs/exp1/text -H "Authorization: Bearer $MODGRAD_TOKEN" --data-binary @-
    curl -X POST $OBS/api/v1/runs/exp1/finish -H "Authorization: Bearer $MODGRAD_TOKEN" -d '{"exit_code": 0}'
    curl "$OBS/api/index"                                       # runs (a project token scopes it)
    curl "$OBS/api/v1/runs/exp1/history?keys=loss,acc&stride=10" # {"steps", "t", "columns"}

The first `log` creates the run. `step` is optional (default: last + 1).
Nested objects flatten with `/`. Re-sending a row is harmless. With a
project token, a run id without `/` lands in the token's project.

## SSH (nothing to install)

On a server started with `modgrad-server --ssh <addr>`, a training script's
output can go straight to a run with only an SSH client:

    python train.py 2>&1 | ssh obs.example.org               # new run, auto-named
    python train.py 2>&1 | ssh obs.example.org run exp1      # run exp1
    ssh obs.example.org runs                                 # this key's runs
    ssh obs.example.org tail exp1                            # latest values
    ssh obs.example.org token                                # a project token for the other doors

The output is echoed back unchanged and metric lines are parsed as by
`modgrad run`; the dashboard URL is printed first (stderr). EOF finishes the
run; a dropped connection leaves it unfinished. The SSH key is the account:
the same key always lands in the same anonymous project; there is no signup.
`token` prints an `obsp_` token on stdout and, on stderr, the matching
`modgrad init --server ... --token ...` and curl lines, so the CLI, Python
and HTTP doors can write to the same project. Prefer `modgrad init` when
you can install it: it spools when the server is unreachable and samples
CPU/GPU; the SSH pipe does neither.

## Framework snippets

With the Python client installed, use its integrations; they write local
runs in local mode and post to the server otherwise:

    from modgrad.integrations.huggingface import ModgradCallback   # Trainer(..., report_to="none", callbacks=[ModgradCallback(project="sft")])
    from modgrad.integrations.lightning import ModgradLogger       # L.Trainer(logger=ModgradLogger(project="pretrain"))

Without the client, the snippets below post to the HTTP API with
`requests`; each logging call is one small POST. Set `MODGRAD_URL` (and `MODGRAD_TOKEN` unless the server runs `--dev`).
Never let logging crash training: catch and drop errors.

    import os, requests
    OBS = os.environ.get("MODGRAD_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8790")
    HDR = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['MODGRAD_TOKEN']}"} if os.environ.get("MODGRAD_TOKEN") else {}

    def obs_log(run, step, metrics, **envelope):
        """envelope: config={...}, events=[...], summary={...}, finish=True"""
        body = dict(envelope)
        if metrics:   # step=None means "one past the run's last step"
            body["rows"] = [{**metrics, **({"step": step} if step is not None else {})}]
        try:
            requests.post(f"{OBS}/api/v1/runs/{run}/log", json=body, headers=HDR, timeout=5)
        except requests.RequestException:
            pass

PyTorch loop:

    obs_log("exp1", 0, {}, config={"lr": lr, "batch_size": bs})
    for step, batch in enumerate(loader):
        loss = model(batch).loss
        loss.backward(); opt.step(); sched.step(); opt.zero_grad()
        if step % 10 == 0:
            obs_log("exp1", step, {"train/loss": loss.item(), "lr": sched.get_last_lr()[0]})
    obs_log("exp1", step, {"val/loss": evaluate(model)}, finish=True)

Hugging Face Trainer:

    from transformers import TrainerCallback

    class ObsCallback(TrainerCallback):
        def __init__(self, run):
            self.run = run
        def on_train_begin(self, args, state, control, **kw):
            if state.is_world_process_zero:
                obs_log(self.run, 0, {}, config=args.to_sanitized_dict())
        def on_log(self, args, state, control, logs=None, **kw):
            if state.is_world_process_zero and logs:
                obs_log(self.run, state.global_step, logs)   # non-numeric values are skipped
        def on_train_end(self, args, state, control, **kw):
            if state.is_world_process_zero:
                obs_log(self.run, state.global_step, {}, finish=True)

    trainer = Trainer(..., callbacks=[ObsCallback("sft/run1")])

(Or no code at all: `modgrad run --name sft/run1 -- python train.py` parses the
dicts the Trainer prints.)

PyTorch Lightning:

    from lightning.pytorch.loggers.logger import Logger
    from lightning.pytorch.utilities import rank_zero_only

    class ObsLogger(Logger):
        def __init__(self, run):
            super().__init__()
            self._run = run
        @property
        def name(self): return "modgrad"
        @property
        def version(self): return self._run
        @rank_zero_only
        def log_hyperparams(self, params, *a, **kw):
            params = params if isinstance(params, dict) else vars(params)
            obs_log(self._run, 0, {}, config={k: (v if isinstance(v, (int, float, str, bool)) else str(v)) for k, v in params.items()})
        @rank_zero_only
        def log_metrics(self, metrics, step=None):
            obs_log(self._run, step, metrics)
        @rank_zero_only
        def finalize(self, status):
            obs_log(self._run, 0, {}, summary={"status": status}, finish=True)

    trainer = L.Trainer(logger=ObsLogger("pretrain/run1"))

Rust (modgrad SDK): `modgrad_obs::Run::create(...)` and `run.log_scalars(step, &[("loss", x)])`
write the same directory format with no server.

## Viewing

    modgrad-server --root obs                # then open http://127.0.0.1:8790/
    # boards from make_board open at http://127.0.0.1:8790/#board=<id>

The dashboard comes from obs/web/dist in the modgrad checkout (build it once,
see "Build" in obs/web/README.md); `modgrad-server` says on startup where it
serves it from. Add `--dev` to accept writes without a token.
